20822-the-camp-fire-girls-on-the-march-o:
Hard feeling from the camp next door sours a stay in Bessie King's Test of Friendship. Jane L. Stewart, in this 1914 Camp Fire Girls tale, has Bessie reflect that things ended well. Had rival girls had their way, no pleasant memory would remain.

Camp Fire Girls, a real movement for American girls, fills these tales with hikes and service. Bessie King leads her friends through tests of loyalty and nerve. The march of the title brings outdoor trials and tests of character. Stewart's set shows how fiction spread the Camp Fire ideals of health, work, and outdoor joy.
22479-the-psychical-researcher-s-tale-th:
J. D. Beresford wrote The Psychical Researcher's Tale, subtitled The Sceptical Poltergeist. It appeared in the New Decameron among tales of mixed kinds. Beresford's researcher investigates a household troubled by a poltergeist.

Cases of the type reach back to John Wesley's days, he notes. The Slippertons kept a fat, very stupid cook at the house. The researcher suspected her of being an unconscious medium for the disturbances. The family, though, were attached to her and refused his advice. They would not give her notice, as he strongly urged. That deadlock gives the tale its comic, sceptical edge. Readers get ghost-hunting told with wit rather than terror.
cantillon-essai-commerce-1755-fr:
Richard Cantillon's Essai sur la nature du commerce en général appeared in 1755, in French, after his death. No public-domain English translation exists in this entry's line, so the text stands in French. Cantillon, an Irish banker in Paris, wrote the first systematic treatise on economics, before Adam Smith.

Cantillon traced value to land and labor, followed money through an economy, and pictured trade as a flow between town and country. His portrait of the entrepreneur, who buys at known prices and sells at unknown ones, still defines the word's use in economics. Smith and later writers drew on him quietly. The Essai earns its place as the quiet start of economic science.

durkheim-division-travail-social-1893-fr:
Émile Durkheim published De la division du travail social in 1893, in French. The work was his doctoral thesis and the first major statement of his thought. No public-domain English translation exists, so the text stands here in its original language.

Durkheim argued that the division of labor does more than make goods: it binds society together. Older societies held by likeness, he said, while modern ones hold by difference and mutual need. He called those bonds mechanical and organic solidarity. The thesis founded his career and helped make sociology a science of its own, with society itself, not the lone person, as its object.
durkheim-formes-elementaires-1912-fr:
Émile Durkheim published Les Formes élémentaires de la vie religieuse in 1912, in French. No public-domain English translation exists, so the text stands here in its original language. The book, on the elementary forms of religious life, was his deepest work on religion and society.

Durkheim studied totemism among Aboriginal peoples of Australia, which he took as religion's simplest form. He argued that when a clan worships its totem, it is really worshipping itself as a society. The sacred, then, is society pictured in symbols. That claim founded the sociology of religion and still drives debate on ritual, symbols, and the ties that hold groups together.
durkheim-regles-methode-1895-fr:
Émile Durkheim published Les Règles de la méthode sociologique in 1895, in French. No public-domain English translation exists, so the text stands here in French. The short book is a manifesto: it tells the new science of sociology how it must work if it wants to be a science at all.

Durkheim's first rule was to treat social facts as things, as real as rocks or weather, and to study them from outside. Customs, laws, and beliefs press on each person whether we like them or not. He set rules for proof, comparison, and the sorting of normal from sick societies. The manifesto gave the field its method and its confidence.
durkheim-suicide-1897-fr:
Émile Durkheim published Le Suicide in 1897, in French, a study of suicide built on official statistics. No public-domain English translation exists, so the text stands here in French. Durkheim chose a topic that seemed the most private act of all, to prove that society shapes even it.

Rates of suicide, he showed, stayed steady for each group yet differed sharply by faith, family, and social tie. He sorted suicides into types, including the egoistic and the altruistic, each tied to how strongly society held the person. The work founded quantitative sociology, the use of numbers to prove that social facts are real forces in human lives.
nasa-tm-19630012631-a-study-of-cryopump-:
J. O. Ballance, W. K. Roberts, and D. W. Tarbell of Marshall wrote this study on June 27, 1962. It treats cryopumps, pumps that freeze gas onto very cold surfaces. The setting is free molecular flow, where air is too thin to flow smoothly. Ground test chambers use such pumps to mimic space vacuum.

The abstract begins with the share of gas a cold surface can catch. A Monte Carlo computer method modeled how molecules strike and stick. Shape matters: a well-aimed cold trap catches far more gas. The team compared layouts to find which shapes focus molecules best. Better vacuum chambers meant truer tests of spacecraft before flight.
nasa-tm-19690016178-predicted-and-actual:
Thomas J. Karras and Ralph E. Taylor wrote this Goddard preprint, numbered X-560-69-147, comparing predicted and actual spacecraft radio interference. A craft's own circuits can spray radio noise into its telemetry stream home. The team made a first attempt to check interference forecasts against what tracking stations observed and what data teams recovered.

They studied three November 1968 days for the IMP-F spacecraft and examined ten recorded station tapes. A high degree of match was found, with interference verified in eight of the ten tapes. About three percent of the craft's telemetry data was badly degraded, they report. A small share was lost outright, and the rest arrived in poor shape.
nasa-tm-19720020239-detection-of-interpl:
T L Cline and colleagues reported these electron detections in a NASA preprint numbered X-666-72-221. Spacecraft found a quiet time flow of electrons between the planets. Their energies sat above the solar wind's and below true cosmic rays. The energy spectrum fell steadily across the measured range. It spanned from eighteen thousand to nearly two million electron volts. One bump in the spectrum drew special attention.

That feature sat between one hundred and three hundred thousand electron volts. The paper's first part asks where such electrons come from. Finding a steady background flow changed ideas about interplanetary space. Even in quiet times, the space between planets is not empty of energetic particles. The authors weighed solar and planetary sources for the flow.
proudhon-confessions-revolutionnaire-185:
P.-J. Proudhon told his own story in Les Confessions d'un revolutionnaire, printed in French in 1851. The revolutionary's confession mixes autobiography with theory. Proudhon had sat in the assembly during the February Revolution of 1848. His narrative runs from that hopeful rising to the coup that crushed the republic.

He explains his famous claims on property and his clashes with rivals and rulers. Prison and exile marked the path his confession records. No public domain English translation exists, so the French text stands alone. Readers meet the first self named anarchist in his own words. The book is both a life and a brief for his cause.
quesnay-oeuvres-economiques-philosophiqu:
Auguste Oncken edited the complete economic and philosophical works of Francois Quesnay in 1888. Quesnay, doctor to the French king, founded the physiocratic school of economics. His Tableau economique, a famous diagram of how wealth flows, leads the system. Land and farming stand at its source, in his scheme.

The French edition gathers his essays, dialogues, and maxims in one critical volume. No public domain English translation exists, so the French original stands as the record. Physiocracy shaped Turgot and influenced Adam Smith's generation. Readers with French meet the school's founder whole. The Tableau alone repays the effort of the language.
the-lights-of-the-church-and-the-light-o: Huxley's essay on the lights of the church and the light of science: faith and knowledge compared. The agnostic's challenge, eloquently put. A classic of the science-religion debate, a classic of the great debate.
